brief_copy.job: Standalone Tuesday broadcast telling the full comparison story and connecting the decision standard to ELEVATE. Use one reply invitation, no audit CTA and no claim that this client belongs to ELEVATE.
brief_copy.body:
Building something new can make the next decision seem obvious. The page is ready, the team has done the work, and switching traffic over can look like the natural next step.

But the fact that we created an alternative doesn't settle whether it should replace what's already there.

**We owe our own work the same scrutiny we give the work a client brings to us.**

In that conversation, I also described changes we planned to make to our page. Once those updates were made, I said I would send it back so the client could review it again.

Our version was something we were prepared to keep working on, rather than something the client's advertising had to accommodate because we'd built it.

If you've invested in your wedding business's marketing, you want a team that understands the value of that investment. You're hiring us to contribute expertise, make recommendations and give you clear reasoning for the decisions we take with your ads.

That includes distinguishing between having a new page available and having a reason to change where couples go after clicking.

We can bring a strong recommendation and still be open to improving our contribution. Respect for your existing work belongs alongside confidence in what we create.

It's the kind of judgment we bring to ELEVATE, our full-service advertising management program. The value of having an advertising team includes how we evaluate our own work, not only what we deliver.
brief_copy.ending:
Reply to this email, and let's see what the right next step looks like.

Talk soon,
Whitney

content.title: A page we build should face the same scrutiny as the page you already use

slides.job: State the promise as an insight about the reader's advertising.
slides.text:
A page we build should face the same scrutiny as the page you already use.

When your advertising team creates a new landing page, that gives your business another option. It doesn't automatically settle where your ad traffic should go. The decision to replace an existing destination needs its own reasoning, even when we're the team behind the alternative.

slides.job: Introduce the single comparison scene without publishing performance information.
slides.text:
In a client conversation, we discussed a landing page our team had created alongside the pages the client was already using.

We had compared those options rather than moving every ad visitor to our page at once. The existing pages remained part of the decision instead of being treated as something to remove simply because a new version was available.

slides.job: Explain Whitney's rationale, keeping the actor exact.
slides.text:
Whitney explained why we had taken that approach: we wanted to know how the new page would convert before switching everything over.

Creating the page was our contribution. Deciding whether it should replace the other destinations was a separate responsibility. Giving our own work proper consideration also meant giving the client's existing work a fair place in that evaluation.

slides.job: Show that WIA's work remained open to refinement; preserve planned tense.
slides.text:
The next part of the conversation concerned our page.

Whitney outlined revisions we planned to make, then said she would return it to the client for another look. That kept the responsibility with us to refine what we'd created, while leaving room for the client's review before the revised version moved forward.

slides.job: Connect the scene to an established owner's expectations of a partner.
slides.text:
You may be bringing an ads team into a business with years of thought already invested in its marketing.

You want their expertise and a clear recommendation. You also want them to understand what they're being asked to build on. A thoughtful partner can introduce something new without treating the existing work as disposable or making replacement the measure of their contribution.

slides.job: State WIA's belief without claiming a universal testing protocol.
slides.text:
**Our authorship shouldn't give a page an advantage in the decision.**

We can stand behind the work we create while remaining willing to compare it, revise it and reconsider the role it should play. That is part of serving the client's advertising well. The business deserves a recommendation based on the job the page needs to do for couples, rather than whose page it is.

slides.job: Close for both management and guided-support readers without an explicit ask.
slides.text:
Whether you want us to manage your advertising or launch your campaigns and guide you while you run them, you deserve the same care in our recommendations.

Our role is to bring expertise to your business while respecting what you've already built. New work should add a considered option to your advertising, with a clear reason for the place we recommend it takes.

caption.body:
When a new page is ready, it can feel natural to make it the next destination for your advertising. But an owner has more to consider than whether the team has finished building it. There's also the investment already made in the business's existing pages and the reason for changing their role.

On a client call, we explained why our landing page had been compared with the client's current pages before a full traffic switch. The conversation then turned to revisions we planned for our version and returning it for another review.

That sequence matters because it keeps our work inside the evaluation. We haven't earned a replacement decision solely by producing the replacement.

As your advertising partner, we want to bring a clear point of view without making the business conform to whatever we've most recently created. Sometimes the useful contribution is another option and a considered comparison, followed by more work on that option.

You can expect us to take our own recommendations seriously enough to examine the work behind them, while recognising the value of what's already in place.
caption.hook: A delivery milestone shouldn't decide where couples land after an ad.
caption.ending: That gives the partnership room for new ideas without making a change of ownership the reason to change your advertising.

brief_copy.title: Our landing page wasn't an automatic replacement
brief_copy.script:
We built a landing page for a client, and we didn't move all their ad traffic to it.

A little context. They already had pages in their advertising, and we'd created another option. But building that option didn't automatically answer the question of where we should send couples.

On the call, I explained why we were comparing our page with the existing pages instead of switching everything over. We wanted to understand how our version would convert before making that change.

And I also told the client we were going to make updates to our page and send it back so they could take another look.

I think that matters when you're trusting someone with your advertising. You're bringing us in to make thoughtful decisions for your business, and sometimes that means taking another look at something our own team created.

We can believe in the page we've built and still give the pages you already have a fair comparison. Those two things can exist together.

What I want you to feel is that we're looking after your advertising, including being willing to improve our contribution before asking it to take the place of yours.

caption.body:
You've already put thought into how couples discover your business and where they go to learn more. When you bring in an advertising partner, you want that investment to be understood as the team considers what to add or change.

In one client conversation, I explained a decision involving a landing page we'd created. We were comparing it with the pages already being used rather than directing every ad click to our version simply because we'd built it.

I also outlined updates we planned to make before bringing the page back to the client for another review. Our contribution was open to refinement, just like anything else in the advertising.

That's an important part of how I think about the responsibility we're taking on. A team can have a clear recommendation without assuming every new asset should immediately replace an existing one. The reasoning has to serve the wedding business, including the couples considering it.

You should be able to see that care in the decisions we make about our own work, as well as the work we inherit.

I had a call with a client recently about a landing page our team had built. They already had pages in their advertising, and we'd created another option. But building that option didn't automatically answer the question of where we should send couples.

On the call, I explained why we were comparing our page with the existing pages instead of switching everything over. We wanted to understand how our version would convert before making that change.

Our work should earn its place in your advertising, with the same scrutiny we give the work already there.

I think that matters when you're trusting someone with your advertising. You're bringing us in to make thoughtful decisions for your business, and sometimes that means taking another look at something our own team created.

We can believe in the page we've built and still give the pages you already have a fair comparison. Those two things can exist together.

What I want you to feel is that we're looking after your advertising, including being willing to improve our contribution before asking it to take the place of yours.

caption.body:
For a wedding business, a page is part of the path a couple takes from discovering you to making an inquiry. Choosing where to send that couple deserves more consideration than who created the newest option.

We discussed exactly that in a client call. Our team had built a landing page, but the decision was to compare it with the client's existing pages before making a complete switch. Whitney then described refinements we intended to make and a further opportunity for the client to review our version.

That moment shows the distinction between delivering an asset and deciding the role it should play. The page can be finished enough to evaluate without becoming the automatic destination for every ad.

We want our recommendations to reflect the business we're advertising, rather than a preference for replacing what was there with something of our own. That includes being prepared to revisit our contribution when we're considering the next decision.

An owner should feel that new expertise is being applied with respect for their existing work and care for where their advertising goes next.
